subject: Standby-to-active lag causing p95/p99 spikes — FinLytics escalation
messages:
From: Anita Rao <anita@finlytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, May 7, 2028 at 09:12 AM -0700
Subject: Latency spikes tied to scale-ups (p95/p99 regressions)

Hi Marissa,

We started seeing elevated p95/p99 latency this morning (around 08:30 PDT) that lines up with autoscaler spin-ups for our peak traffic windows. The problem looks intermittent but reproducible: when a new GPU is provisioned and assigned, our tail latency jumps from ~120ms p99 to ~850–1,100ms for a short period (2–6 minutes) and correlates with a rise in error rate for long-running chat requests.

I've attached a trimmed trace and sample requests (finlytics-p99-sample-0507.json.gz). We rely on Redwood hosted API for real-time scoring and this behavior is hitting SLAs. Can you triage urgently and tell us what mitigation you can apply? We need an estimate for a fix and any immediate mitigations (pre-warm, scheduled capacity, credits).

Thanks,
Anita Rao
Head of Engineering
FinLytics

2) If it’s a load-after-ready race, we will push a targeted mitigation (keep-one-warm) to the pool and roll a canary.

Subject: Re: Latency spikes tied to scale-ups (p95/p99 regressions) — initial triage

Hey all — quick update from triage. I pulled the sample and our infra traces for your pool (FinLytics-prod-usw). Observations:

- The p99 spikes align precisely with new instance allocations (scale-up events).
- The timeline shows GPU provisioning -> driver ready -> container created -> model artifact fetch -> model load -> first request. In ~40% of observed events, the first request is routed before the model load completes, causing synchronous load-on-request and the ~800–1,200ms tail.
- The model artifact size and cold-load time are within expected range, but our allocation path currently allows request traffic to the instance once the GPU is reachable, not after model is fully loaded. That race is the likely root cause.

Immediate mitigations we can apply within the hour:
- Keep-one-warm: maintain a single warm instance per pool so scale-ups seldom hit a fully-cold slot.
- Readiness gating: change routing to ensure the instance only receives requests after model load completes (requires a short rollout).
- Client-side workaround: staggered retries and 503 handling for first request after scale-up.

I’m attaching a visual trace (init-lag-trace-0507.svg) that shows the gap. I’ll open a jira and propose a hotfix to gate routing on model readiness.

—Rishi
SRE, Redwood Inference

Anita — thank you for escalating. I’m sorry for the disruption; we take SLA impacts seriously. I’ve summarized the impact and initial remediation plan below and requested an internal exec sync to prioritize the fix and credit discussion.

Summary (TL;DR):
- Root cause (triage): request routing can reach instances before model artifacts finish loading — results in synchronous model load on first request post-scale-up.
- Immediate mitigations: apply keep-one-warm in FinLytics-prod-usw pool (deployable now), and roll readiness gate (hotfix) to prevent routing until model load completes (canary same day).
- Next steps: Rishi to open INF-2347, target canary in 6–8 hours, full rollout after canary validation.

Proposed exec sync: Today 2:00 PM PT — we’ll include a short timeline for credits and follow-up KPI reporting (p95/p99 by route). I’m attaching a one-page mutual action plan (MAP_v1_FinLytics.pdf) with proposed checkpoints.

We’ll also temporarily apply a conservative autoscaler cushion for your prod pool to reduce allocation churn while we validate fixes.

—Marissa
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Subject: INF-2347 root cause & hotfix plan

Update from engineering: we opened INF-2347 (https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INF-2347). Root cause: a race in the allocation controller where routing marks the instance Ready once the GPU driver returns OK; the model artifact fetch and load are kicked off asynchronously but are not awaited before routing. Fix: (A) gating readiness on model load completion, (B) a short-term keep-one-warm to reduce cold allocations.

Canary plan:
- Canary scope: FinLytics-prod-usw pool only.
- Timeline: deploy hotfix to canary at 21:00 PT tonight, monitor for 2 hours. If canary reduces p99 on alloc events by >=70% and no regression in overall latency, expand to 30% of pool, then full rollout over next 6 hours.
- Expected impact: p99 for allocation windows should drop from ~900–1,200ms to ~150–250ms (based on local tests with seeded artifacts).

I’ll push the canary and update logs/metrics to the Drive folder. Will also provide a post-canary telemetry snapshot.

—Rishi
SRE, Redwood Inference
